## The Case of the Creaking Knees

The city never sleeps, and neither does your body when you've been sitting too long. I stumbled into this gym at midnight, shadows stretching across the treadmills like alibis that don't quite add up. Every step on that belt was a confession, burning off the sins of the couch potato life.

## A Heart Full of Smoke

They say your heart's a pump, but in this town, it's more like a witness that's seen too much. Running makes it race, lifting makes it thud against your ribs like a fist on a suspect's door. You can feel it, that old rhythm coming back, the one that was there before the sedentary life started its slow poison.

## The Weights Don't Lie

Dumbbells don't talk, but they sure tell the truth. Each rep's a testimony, each set's a deposition under oath. By the time you're done, you're not the same person who walked in—either stronger, or you've learned what weakness really feels like when it's staring back at you from the mirror in the rearview.
